items.summary: On October 24, 2026, the Bombay High Court allowed godwoman Radhe Maa (Sukhwinder Kaur) to file a suit for protection of her personality rights against allegedly defamatory online content. Justice Abhay Ahuja granted permission under Clause XII of the Letters Patent, required when part of the cause of action arises outside territorial jurisdiction. Advocate Hasmit Trivedi argued that harm was suffered within Mumbai and that Google served local users. The court accepted submissions and permitted leave to sue Google and other respondents.
items.title: Bombay High Court Lets Radhe Maa Sue Google Over Online Content

items.summary: At the UN General Assembly's Third Committee, India's First Secretary Raghoo Puri accused Pakistan of misusing the forum for propaganda and failing to protect its citizens. He urged Pakistani representatives to prioritise welfare over military directives and reaffirmed that Jammu & Kashmir is an integral part of India. This followed a rebuke on October 23 regarding minority treatment, with New Delhi accusing Islamabad of neglecting vulnerable communities while lecturing India.
items.title: India Raps Pakistan Over Minority Rights at UN

items.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer visited Port Milwaukee to observe how President Trump's tariffs have affected the flow of goods and impacted the regional economy. The piece frames the situation as whiplash, suggesting disruption from shifting trade policy. NPR notes it does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews, warning that anyone making such an offer is not an employee.
items.title: Reporter Visits Port Milwaukee on Tariff Impact

items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, an open small language model aimed at local voice assistants, game characters and robot interfaces running on RTX, Jetson and Spark hardware. The model is post-trained from Google's Gemma 4 E4B using reinforcement learning only, skipping supervised fine-tuning entirely. NVIDIA reports it leads 15 of 21 agent benchmarks in its own NeMo-Gym harness, with an IHEval score of 84.8 versus 67.0 for Gemma 4 E4B and 60.6 for Qwen3.5-4B. It is quantized to a Q4_K_M build targeting about 4GB of VRAM on RTX hardware, though the GGUF file itself is 6.18 GB.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B for Local Voice Agents

items.summary: The article asks how a governing system stays vital after decades in power and answers that China relies on continuous, built-in mechanisms of self-purification, self-perfection, self-renewal and self-improvement. It states plainly that this work never stops, so the Communist Party's self-revolution has no end point, with full and rigorous Party self-governance maintained on an ongoing footing.
items.title: China frames self-revolution as endless mechanism

items.summary: CleanTechnica projects that if Tesla’s unsupervised robotaxi miles keep growing at 20% weekly, the company would pass Waymo nationally in roughly 11 weeks and reach about 10 million weekly miles by week 16. The author notes recent growth from 250,000 to around 3.3 million unsupervised miles and treats that rate as a limited-window scenario against Waymo’s slowing gains and the combined Uber + Lyft volume in Austin, Dallas, and Houston. He frames sustaining the pace for 16 weeks—requiring fleet deployment, geofence expansion, and pricing—as the real question rather than demand, while noting Tesla aims to demonstrate unit economics with revenue expected by 2027.
items.title: Tesla’s Compounding Robotaxi Miles Could Pass Waymo in Weeks

items.summary: Barack Obama threw his support behind Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for US Senate in Michigan, on Saturday at Cass technical high school in Detroit. Obama said El-Sayed was “fighting for change, real change” and would “finish the job we started with the Affordable Care Act.” The rally came on the first day of early voting ahead of the general election on 3 November. El-Sayed had trailed Haley Stevens by about 51% to 45% in August’s primary but leads Mike Rogers statewide, a Marist poll put him at 50% and Rogers at 48%, with RealClearPolitics averaging an about 2.6-point lead for El-Sayed. The Cook Political Report rates the race a toss-up.
items.title: Obama rallies Michigan crowd behind El-Sayed Senate bid

items.summary: Young female politicians in Western Australia say they remain determined to enter politics even as online harassment and misogyny grow, according to a 2024 Australian National University study that ranked fear of such abuse among the top barriers for young women. Youth Parliamentarian Charlotte Rawlinson said she would not let abusers have satisfaction, while Busselton Councillor Mikalya Love described new safety strategies since joining council five years ago. Liberal youth leader Hannah Hutton noted increasing political divisiveness and name-calling. Former prime minister Julia Gillard added that evidence shows abuse against women MPs is rising and more action is needed.
items.title: WA young women stay motivated despite rising political abuse

items.summary: India revised its tax treaty with Mauritius, introducing a Principal Purpose Test (PPT) to block cross-border structures used mainly for unintended tax advantages. The change does not automatically strip benefits from all Mauritian investors. Instead, authorities may examine an arrangement's purpose and deny treaty benefits if securing them was a principal objective.
items.title: India's New PPT Rules for Mauritius Treaty Investors

items.summary: The ARK shelter in Kansai introduced Kumaji, an abandoned dog found wandering near its grounds this spring. He adapted quickly and is described as extremely affectionate toward visitors, walks, and cars, embodying the phrase “bundle of joy.” Estimated to be about 6 or 7 years old, he knows basic commands like sitting so his enthusiasm stays manageable. The shelter hopes he finds a permanent match.
items.title: Shelter dog Kumaji described as lovable people-pleaser seeking a home

items.summary: Tens of thousands gathered at Hostage Square in Tel Aviv for a final protest against Benjamin Netanyahu and his government, three days before the Israeli parliament election on Tuesday. Attendees demanded an independent state commission of inquiry into the October 7 attacks, which they described as Israel's greatest security breach. Opposition leaders including Gadi Eisenkot attended; Prime Minister Netanyahu has flatly refused to establish such a body. Speakers said Netanyahu represents a threat to democracy and called for government change, though one attendee expressed doubt that his removal will occur.
items.title: Tel Aviv protesters demand Netanyahu's ouster before election

items.summary: Anti-establishment demonstrations turned violent across France and Spain on Saturday, with protesters clashing with police while shops were looted and public property damaged. In Barcelona, authorities arrested 100 people after hooded demonstrators vandalised stores around the central Plaza de Catalunya; Catalonia's interior minister Núria Parlon said about a quarter of those detained were minors, added that more than 30 fires were set and 14 shops were vandalised or looted. French police made nearly 1,000 arrests during protests over living costs and school funding.
items.title: Anti-establishment Protests Turn Violent in France and Spain

items.summary: Fixed deposit rates have climbed, with select institutions offering up to 8.35% for senior citizens. Small finance banks and NBFCs generally yield more than large commercial banks, though the top advertised rate may apply only to a specific tenure or investor category. Investors are advised to compare deposit safety, tenure, liquidity and taxation before choosing.
items.title: FD Rates Rise To 8.35% Across Bank Types

items.summary: A journalist visited the Rosebank oil field by helicopter, arriving shortly after the government granted consent for gas from Jackdaw. The floating Petrojarl Rosebank vessel sits 80 miles north west of Shetland and is larger than Jackdaw, with an estimated 300m to 500m barrels enough for perhaps 25 years. Workers describe good conditions; production supervisor Douglas Hogge said approval would see many out to retirement. Environmental campaigners disagree: Tessa Khan of Uplift called it a disastrous decision and urged prime minister Andy Burnham to prioritise renewables. The Court of Session ruled in 2025 that approvals were unlawful over climate impact, though developers may continue work short of production. Sources told BBC News the UK government decision should come before Christmas.
items.title: Journalists visit Rosebank oil field amid UK energy row

items.summary: The Iran war has made oil tanker voyages inefficient, crumbing vessel availability and pushing freight costs to record highs that nearly erase the incentive for shipping crude from the U.S. Gulf Coast to Asia. Freight rates eased from early October peaks but remained about $60 million this week for a supertanker voyage. Asian refiner orders for November delivery plunged by about 50% from September, to about 25 million barrels, anonymous traders told Bloomberg. If low, Asia could receive its lowest U.S. crude volumes in seven years. Valero's Randy Hawkins said VLCC costs averaged around $30-$35 a barrel versus roughly $5 in 2025.
items.title: Record Tanker Rates Cripple U.S. Crude Oil Flows to Asia

items.summary: Former US President Barack Obama criticized Republican figures during a campaign event in Ohio ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. He focused much of his criticism on Vivek Ramaswamy, defending an advertisement featuring Dr Amy Acton, mother of Ramaswamy's Democratic rival. Obama said there is 'no line he will not cross,' while Acton accused him of exploiting her childhood to save his campaign. Obama also criticized President Donald Trump over cost of living and pointed to White House renovation plans instead. He urged voters to reject Republican leadership in the midterms.
items.title: Obama Criticizes Ramaswamy Ad and Trump Over Decency

items.summary: Volkswagen is offering its new electric Jetta M6 sedan in China with nearly 290 miles of CLTC-rated range for less than $12,000. The entry-level 465 Pro version carries a 42.9 kWh battery and a 113 kW motor that the company says reaches 100 km/h in about 8.3 seconds. Built on FAW’s Jiesi architecture as part of a joint venture, it is positioned toward young professionals and families. The writer speculates North American VW dealers might benefit from such an affordable model.
items.title: Volkswagen Launches Low-Cost Chinese Jetta M6 Electric Sedan

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey will include a £1.5bn borrowing facility and an initial £285m “good growth” funding in next week’s budget, alongside Treasury support to help authorities scale up capacity amid fears over their ability to administer larger budgets. The plans were drawn with No 10 North after regional mayors complained about limited borrowing power compared with counterparts abroad.
items.title: Healey’s budget sets out devolution package for English local leaders

items.summary: A public interest litigation filed in the Supreme Court asks the court for guidelines governing how criminal investigation agencies collect and access personal and digital data. The petition requests that requests specify purpose, categories of information sought, relevant time period and connection to an alleged offence, be limited to what is strictly necessary and proportionate, and not be granted routinely when privacy safeguards are absent or less intrusive alternatives remain available. It cites Supreme Court judgments and invokes Articles 14, 19 and 21 of the Constitution to protect rights to privacy, dignity, freedom of speech and expression and personal liberty.
items.title: Supreme Court Plea Seeks Data-Access Guidelines for Probe Agencies

items.summary: Asian shipping fuel costs are rising sharply as high-sulphur fuel oil prices exceed crude feedstock levels, driven by Middle Eastern and Russian supply losses. Singapore's November crack against Dubai crude rose above $10/bbl in mid-October versus a February discount of around $5/bbl, reversing more than $15/bbl for HSFO. Supply disruptions from Hormuz shipping attacks reduced Gulf shipments to 40,000–50,000 b/d while Russian supplies fell to 25,000 b/d by September amid refinery disruptions. Resilient Asian demand and high freight rates sustain the premium despite seasonal relief prospects toward year-end.
items.title: Singapore Fuel Oil Prices Surge Amid Supply Disruption

items.summary: The maiden MP Semiconductor Summit 2026 concluded in Indore on Saturday, having been inaugurated by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Friday. Over seven roundtable meetings focused on building a self-reliant ecosystem for semiconductors, photonics, quantum technology and electronics manufacturing within the state. Anshuman Raj of MPSEDC said the goal was to understand industry needs and explore support through academic institutions and government.
items.title: Indore Semiconductor Summit Sets Chip-Making Roadmap

items.summary: From Tuesday, Oct 27, passengers buying reserved tickets from railway reservation counters can opt for travel insurance. The premium is just 45 paise per passenger and covers Rs 10 lakh in case of death or permanent total disability in a train accident. Normal second class or general class passengers are not covered.
items.title: Indian Railways Offers Cheap Travel Insurance at Reservation Counters From October 27

items.summary: Zhou Wenxing, a commentator for CGTN affiliated with Nanjing University, argues that Taiwan's restoration to China in 1945 is firmly established by history and international law. He contends that some Western politicians have revived the claim that 'Taiwan's status is undetermined,' which he describes as based on selective readings of wartime documents. Wenxing traces a legal chain beginning with the Cairo Declaration, continued through the Potsdam Proclamation and Japan's Instrument of Surrender in 1945, culminating in Taiwan's administration being restored to China. He asserts that subsequent changes in Chinese government did not alter this sovereignty, framing the ongoing dispute as an internal matter rather than a question of territorial ownership.
items.title: Commentator Defends Taiwan's Restoration as Settled Historical Fact

items.summary: Four people were injured in a drive-by shooting outside Fitzys Loganholme on Bryants Road, south of Brisbane, where the Logan City Titles Fight Night was held. Police responded to reports of shots fired from a vehicle at 8.15pm; the involved vehicle left the scene and offenders remain at large. Four injured people were taken to hospital with conditions being assessed.
items.title: Four injured after drive-by shooting outside Brisbane boxing event

items.summary: Great Wines World Tokyo, created by American wine critic James Suckling in 2024, is holding its third edition. The event has grown into a marquee stop on Tokyo's wine calendar, with the previous two editions selling out and this year's also sold out apart from a waitlist. It returns to the Grand Hyatt Tokyo on Nov. 4.
items.title: James Suckling's Great Wines World Tokyo Marks Its Third Edition

items.summary: The Israeli military launched a crackdown in occupied West Bank city of Hebron, demolishing homes and businesses and displacing hundreds of families, according to local officials. Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced, while the governor and deputy mayor said at least 200 families were affected. The operation followed two Israeli soldiers killed in an attack on a checkpoint.
items.title: Israeli forces demolish Hebron homes, displace families

items.summary: On Sunday (Oct 25), air quality across Singapore stayed unhealthy, with the National Environment Agency reporting 24-hour PSI readings of 103 to 138 at 8am. Hourly PM2.5 readings were in the normal band everywhere, ranging from 43 to 55. NEA had earlier forecast Sunday's PSI between 80 and 130, citing southwest or west winds that could limit smoke haze transport.
items.title: Singapore haze stays unhealthy; PM2.5 normal in all regions

items.summary: Studio Terre designer Terence Chan restored an early-20th-century Emerald Hill shophouse in Singapore that the architecture firm Woha had originally converted. The current owner, a professional in his mid-40s who commissioned Chan after discovering Mun Summ’s involvement, wanted to recover the home’s original grace and turn it into an entertainment-focused space. Chan removed cold finishes, reinstated beige stone, cleared teak stains and added pivot doors, glass balustrades and curated art by Noguchi, Degas and others. The project required meeting conservation guidelines and repairing termite damage over a century-old structure. Chan called it “a multi-layered restoration project and a creative playground rolled into one.”
items.title: Woha Shophouse Restored Into Art-Filled Sanctuary

items.summary: Brazilians will vote on Sunday for their next president, choosing between current left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The two candidates are very different. Bolsonaro is the son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, who beat Lula by a narrow margin in the first round of voting on 4 October.
items.title: Brazilian Voters Choose Between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in Presidential Race

items.summary: Large crowds gathered across France to protest issues including school funding and economic inequality, prompting police to deploy heavily in an effort to prevent a repeat of last week's violence.
items.title: French Police Deploy as Protests Renew Across Country

items.summary: Israel's most far-right cabinet minister helped shape hardline policies toward Palestinians in recent years. Benjamin Netanyahu vows to give him a senior position if he is reelected next week, reflecting the minister's influence over the government.
items.title: Israel's Far-Right Minister Gains Netanyahu Support Amid Re-election Push

items.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah reviewed how the Delhi Police handled protests, including allegations of excessive force during the Cockroach Janata Party's Sansad Chalo march and its October 10 Jantar Mantar demonstration. The meeting at police headquarters also covered women's safety, drug trafficking, gangsters abroad, traffic management and traders' concerns over festive-season disruptions.
items.title: Amit Shah Reviews Delhi Police Amid Force Allegations

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed all states and wetland authorities to complete physical verification and demarcation of water bodies within four months. A bench comprising Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M. Pancholi observed that courts cannot remain silent spectators when precious water resources remain unprotected, noting the work remained incomplete even nine years after rules were notified. The court initially proposed a four-week deadline before granting additional time following arguments from senior advocate Shekhar Naphade.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders States To Map Wetlands Within Four Months

items.summary: Luxury and high-street retailers in central Brussels covered their windows with wooden panels on Saturday as fresh protests raised concerns over further unrest, taking precautions against a repeat of the looting that struck the capital a week earlier. Some businesses remained open; at Nike customers could enter through an uncovered doorway, while Quick displayed a small notice reading "open" on its boarded frontage.
items.title: Brussels shops boarded up amid fears of repeat looting

items.summary: A Reuters report, citing six former senior US officials, says the administrations of Joe Biden and Donald Trump repeatedly asked Elon Musk's SpaceX to activate or restrict its Starlink service in various countries. Requests included disabling it for Iran-backed militias in Yemen and Lebanon and enabling it in Iran and Ukraine. The article notes renewed concern after recent restrictions on Ukrainian access to Starshield, which Zelenskiy said were deliberately imposed and slowed drone performance; Musk stated the US government controls such limits. Coverage highlights debates over relying on private satellite infrastructure for national security. Livemint—News Desk delivered the report.
items.title: US Administrations Pressured Musk Over Starlink Controls Abroad

items.summary: Cristian Volpato, a 22-year-old Socceroo who plays for Sassuolo, has become the latest professional athlete to license and monetise an artificial-intelligence version of himself. The video showing him spawning four digital clones is fake but authorised by the real player through Callandor, a California-based AI licensing agent founded in February that also represents Jorginho and Chris Poole. Co-founder Michael Fisk says synthetic twins could be used 24-7 for brand deals. Volpato’s deal follows Neymar licensing his likeness to a Chinese platform in June. Experts warn the technology is hard to detect as regulation lags, while Hyperknown’s William Saunders frames it as consent before others decide about identities.
items.title: Footballer Cristian Volpato licenses his AI likeness

items.summary: This article presents a running list, or 'AI graveyard,' of notable artificial intelligence projects and startups that shut down, pivoted, or missed expectations. It frames the collection as a record of lessons rather than merely a scorecard of failures. The piece notes that about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents, citing S&P Global Market Intelligence. Examples include Relay, which closed in August; Character.ai, which filed for bankruptcy in early October after legal and regulatory troubles; Humane's AI Pin, shut down in February 2025 with assets acquired by HP for $116 million; and Yupp, which ceased operations in March 2026. The article also covers stumbles from larger companies like OpenAI, Apple, Microsoft, and Notion Mail, illustrating that even big players face setbacks as competition intensifies across the industry.
items.title: The AI Graveyard: A Running List of Projects That Failed

items.summary: Euronews reported that hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets of Paris for major demonstrations against the cost of living crisis, rising fuel prices and the broader student movement. The government implemented a strict security protocol after last week's protests were overshadowed by violence. Some clashes occurred this time, with nearly 1,000 people arrested.
items.title: Hundreds of Thousands Protest in Paris Over Cost of Living Crisis

items.summary: Ashoke Sen, an ICTS-Infosys Madhava Chair Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS), Tata Institute of Fundamental Research in Bengaluru, has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal, becoming the first Indian physicist to receive it, per news agency PTI. Established in 1988 and named after Swedish physicist Oskar Klein, the medal recognises distinguished contributions to theoretical physics. Sen is widely regarded as an architect of modern string theory, with work on gravity, black holes and matter's fundamental nature. He delivered the accompanying memorial lecture in Stockholm on October 22.
items.title: Indian physicist Ashoke Sen wins 2026 Oskar Klein Medal

items.summary: Saudi authorities issued a potential danger warning covering Mecca, Jeddah, Taif and Yanbu after the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthis toward Taif and Yanbu on Saturday. Residents were told to proceed to the nearest safe place. The alerts were rescinded minutes later amid ongoing fighting.
items.title: Saudi Arabia Issues Potential Danger Warning for Mecca After Missile Attacks

items.summary: The Ukraine Foreign Policy Committee chief, Oleksander Merezhko, called for the resignation of an unnamed official named Witkoff. Separately, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday that Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to pre-restriction speeds, improving front-line logistics and defense against Shahed drones after more than a week of disruption.
items.title: Ukraine Committee Chief Calls for Witkoff's Resignation Amid Starlink Restoration

items.summary: In a debate hosted by Globo, Jair Bolsonaro led former President Lula earlier this month but polls showed the two candidates about even after their gap narrowed. Both repeated campaign proposals on cost of living, welfare and security while exchanging corruption allegations. Lula defended his government's above-inflation minimum wage increases and said his administration helped millions escape hunger.
items.title: Bolsonaro and Lula Trade Barbs in Final Debate

items.summary: Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal challenged RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over remarks on regime change in India. Speaking at a New Delhi press conference reported by Press Trust of India, Sibal insisted Indians sought political change through democratic means rather than unrest. He dismissed comparisons to upheavals abroad as a 'bogey' and questioned how violence arose during peaceful Jantar Mantar protests. Bhagwat had argued such agitations rarely resolve fundamental problems. Sibal countered that unemployment and lack of educational opportunity for the poor were pressing concerns, while also accusing the RSS of past involvement in government change.
items.title: Kapil Sibal Rejects Bhagwat's Regime Change Warning, Urges Democratic Means

items.summary: Air India, IndiGo and Akasa Air extended suspensions of flights to and from several Saudi cities amid an evolving regional security situation. Air India and Air India Express suspended services between Riyadh and Dammam until November 7, 2026, with Jeddah connections remaining suspended until October 31. IndiGo kept cancellations for Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until October 31, while Akasa extended suspensions to Jeddah through November 10 and Riyadh through November 30. The airlines offered flexible rebooking and full refunds for eligible passengers, with revised travel due by late November. IndiGo cited passenger safety as its priority. India's Consulate General in Jeddah issued an advisory to assist affected nationals.
items.title: Indian Airlines Extend Flight Suspensions to Saudi Arabia Amid Security Concerns

items.summary: The website Econvitals is presented as a tracker of mostly U.S. economic indicators, attributed to Jason Furman in the item's first sentence. The text then points readers to the site itself and offers links to subscribe to briefings and read a thread on the platform.
items.title: Econvitals tracks U.S. economic indicators, per Jason Furman

items.summary: Bengaluru Police arrested Delhi man Ritesh Pandey on Saturday for uploading a video targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah. He was later granted bail by the metropolitan magistrate court to cooperate with investigators examining whether he acted at the direction of someone linked to the Janata Dal (Secular) social media team. The case began after Siddaramaiah filed a complaint calling the footage fabricated and part of a blackmail attempt, while his son Yathindra suggested possible Congress involvement in obtaining a ticket.
items.title: Delhi Man Arrested Over Siddaramaiah Video, Granted Bail as JDS Link Probed

items.summary: The Congress high command reportedly asked the Karnataka government to probe alleged sting operation attempts on Chief Ministers D K Shivakumar and V D Satheesan, party sources said. The direction follows Shivakumar's claim that a businessman wearing Meta glasses met him under suspicious circumstances while discussing politics instead of business. He also flagged similar concerns about Cabinet colleagues.
items.title: Congress Asks Karnataka To Probe Alleged Sting Bids On Two CMs

items.summary: Graffiti reading 'Free Umar Khalid' and 'Long Live Naxalbari' appeared on Jawaharlal Nehru University walls in Delhi, sparking a campus controversy. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad unit objected to the writings and alleged Left-wing groups were involved alongside a portrait of VD Savarkar, though these claims have not been independently established. The JNU administration is examining the matter while questions remain over who wrote it.
items.title: JNU Graffiti Row Over Free Umar Khalid and Naxalbari Slogans Sparks Controversy

items.summary: Over the last three years, Indian equities have struggled to outperform inflation or deliver double-digit returns. The benchmark Nifty 50 TRI's compounded return stood at 6.7 per cent versus CPI inflation of 4.1 per cent, while an SBI fixed deposit would have yielded 6.5 per cent over the same period. Investment Trusts and REITs are presented as securities that beat inflation with double-digit returns and lower risk than pure equities. The article lists seven publicly-traded trusts analysed here — PGInvIT, IndiGrid InvIT, Embassy REIT, Mindspace REIT, Brookfield REIT, Nexus REIT and IRB InvIT — each with a listed history of at least three years.
items.title: Indian REITs and InvITs beat inflation over three years

items.summary: Parag Parikh Conservative Hybrid Fund (PCHF) has ranked among the top-performing funds in the Conservative Hybrid Fund category since launching in May 2021. Over five years it delivered a compounded annualised return of 8.4 per cent against 6.1 per cent for the category average, managing assets worth ₹3,454 crore as of September 2026. Its three-pronged approach combines conservative debt with selective low-beta equity and REITs. Three-year rolling returns averaged 11 per cent versus 8.5 per cent for the category. The base expense ratio is 0.54 per cent, lower than the 1.5 per cent average. The fund notes its positioning may limit upside in strong bull markets while offering stability during corrections.
items.title: Parag Parikh Conservative Hybrid Fund Ranks Among Top Performers Since Launch

items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned an attack near Hamoud Church in the southern Jordanian governorate of Karak that killed at least nine people. Moscow called it a 'cynical terrorist act' aimed at undermining interfaith peace and expressed solidarity with Jordan, offering sincere condolences to its leadership, victims' families and friends.
items.title: Russia Condemns Church Attack in Jordan's Karak, Calls It Cynical Terrorist Act

items.summary: The death of Kavantissa, one of Sri Lanka's most iconic wild tuskers, from a gunshot injury triggered public grief and criticism of wildlife authorities. Despite intensive veterinary efforts, he suffered cardiac arrest on Oct. 16 after his condition deteriorated in late September and October. Social media users questioned the care provided, with some alleging negligence or an antibiotic overdose, though such claims require evidence. A court-ordered post-mortem is expected to establish cause of death. Conservationist Prithiviraj Fernando used the reaction to highlight human-elephant conflict, noting Sri Lanka recorded 455 wild elephant deaths in 2025, down from 488 in 2023 and around 388 in 2024. He urged protecting elephants broadly rather than relying on individual surveillance or guarding tuskers after his death.
items.title: Sri Lanka Mourns Iconic Tusker Amid Calls Over Elephant Protection

items.summary: Moscow warned it would deliver a firm response after Moldova declared a Russian embassy staff member persona non grata, calling the move a hostile action. President Maia Sandu said Chisinau cited an alleged Geran drone violation. Russia claimed no evidence supports the drone's origin and accused Moldova of expelling diplomats on fabricated pretexts.
items.title: Russia Warns of Firm Response After Moldova Expels Diplomat

items.summary: Student leader Neha Bora said on Saturday they will not sign a peace bond to maintain order, directing it was contradictory to their right to dissent. The Delhi High Court had rejected the All India Students' Association president's petition challenging the notice issued by a special executive magistrate invoking sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita. Bora said protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar must not be treated as threats, reported PTI.
items.title: AISA's Neha Bora Refuses Peace Bond After Delhi Court Rejects Challenge

items.summary: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah said Pakistan has saved Kashmiris by keeping the issue alive internationally, questioning whether they can expect justice from India. He urged Kashmiris to confront Delhi and affirmed their Indian identity while alleging Muslim oppression in BJP-led states. The Jammu and Kashmir BJP called his remarks seditious and anti-national, demanding police action.
items.title: Farooq Abdullah's pro-Pakistan remark sparks political row over Kashmir

items.summary: In the second T20 International at Christchurch on Oct 24, Tilak Varma produced an unbeaten 51 off just 26 balls to help India chase down a target of 181 runs. His partner Nitish Kumar Reddy added an unbeaten 26 off 13 deliveries, and the two built an unbroken seventh-wicket stand that reached 69 runs off 30 balls before reaching 181 for six in 19.5 overs. India had slumped to 70 for five after Mitchell Santner took four wickets for 21 runs, but Varma and Reddy steadied the chase with support from Naman Dhir (31 off 17 balls) and Abhishek Sharma (27 off 21 balls). Arshdeep Singh was India's most successful bowler earlier in New Zealand's innings, returning two for 33 as they posted 180 for five. PTI reported the four-wicket victory completed a comeback that had looked unlikely when five wickets had fallen.
items.title: Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy guide India past New Zealand in Christchurch

items.summary: The article surveys a growing number of artificial-intelligence agents that users can reach through ordinary text messages instead of separate apps, noting they can remember context and complete tasks such as scheduling appointments or sending emails. It lists many options spanning general-purpose assistants to family- and work-focused tools, including Ask Proxy, Caddy, Comma, Fambot, Folk, Instinct, Iris, Martin, Maverick, Miso, Ohai, Ollie, Orbits, Pally, Poke, Rene, Skye, Stanley, Szn, Tab, Tomo, Town, Underdog, Wajo and Fo. Several carry pricing details, while others are free or open source during beta periods; Instinct is highlighted for its $10 billion valuation after a September 2026 funding round of $1 billion. The piece frames these as notable options so far rather than verified leaders.
items.title: A Roundup of AI Agents That Live in Text Messages

items.summary: Three former hostages returned to Bangui aboard a United Nations flight after roughly ten months of captivity, having been held by Azandé militants since December on election day. A local government official and two National Election Authority members, they were greeted as heroes at a ceremony where sub-prefect Koumba Ndiaye described their ordeal in the bush as extremely difficult.
items.title: Former hostages welcomed home in Bangui

items.summary: It emerged that more than a third of post offices within the troubled TG Jones chain are closing. So far this year 36 branches formerly known as WH Smith have closed and a further 34 are set to close by early 2027, according to Post Office records analysed by the Guardian. Up to 150 of the 450 stores acquired by Modella are expected to shut, about 65 of which have already closed and at least another 46 are to cease operating early next year. This total of 110 announced closures include the 70 containing post offices. The CWU said the closures would leave some areas as “postal deserts”. The Post Office said it is committed to replacing every branch that closes and working quickly through applications from interested postmasters.
items.title: Post Office Closes Over a Third of TG Jones Branches by Early 2027

items.summary: Japanese Foreign Ministry officials visited Moscow this week trying to reach Yuki Imai, a Hokkaido Shimbun correspondent arrested October 14 by the FSB in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk on spying allegations. A court ordered pretrial detention until at least December 12; if convicted he faces up to 20 years. The Japanese embassy has been denied access. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi condemned the arrest and rejected the spy claim, while Russian Ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev said Imai was caught 'red-handed.' DW analysts Yoji Gomi and Stephen Nagy offered differing views on Japan's likely response amid worsening bilateral relations over disputed islands.
items.title: Japan Seeks Access as Russia Detains Journalist Amid Strained Ties

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that Canada and the European Union both retreated from their vehicle emissions commitments this week. In Canada, Electric Autonomy notes a three-year freeze on mandates through 2029, while the federal government still targets 75 percent of new car sales being electric by 2035; Mark Carney and Doug Ford issued a joint statement citing trade pressures. Clean Energy Canada warned the pause could undermine later progress, and Pembina Institute called it nearly impossible to meet EV goals. In Europe, Handelsblatt reports centrist parties may lower the EU's zero-emissions target from 100 percent to as low as 87.5 percent by 2035. The author concludes that short-term concerns keep interfering with long-term climate commitments.
items.title: Canada and EU Delay Vehicle Emissions Commitments Amid Political Turmoil

items.summary: Front-month Brent futures have risen above $116/bbl, nearing the level seen in 2022. Analyst Robin Brooks attributes much of the increase to a large risk premium tied to expectations that a 'hot' war could resume after midterm elections. He notes markets may now place greater weight on supply disruptions than before.
items.title: Brent Futures Approach 2022 Peak on Risk Premium

items.summary: In Global Voices' October 2026 Spotlight, "Big Tech and Authoritarianism," expert Mikhail Doroshevich explains why Belarus's government does not block Western social media. Unlike Russia, whose internet has had independent international connections since the 1990s, Belarus relies on state-controlled infrastructure that is more restricted yet less censored online. The regime uses platforms to spread propaganda and monitors users directly with Russian profiling tools, punishing people for likes or comments. Doroshevich argues these measures are unjustifiable: they increase repression without improving security.
items.title: Big Tech and authoritarian states: Belarus

items.summary: FIFA has formally opened a tender for the media rights to broadcast and stream the men's 2030 World Cup in the United States, with bids due by November 19. This is the first open sale of these U.S. rights since 2011. The tournament will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, while FIFA also allows combined offers for the 2034 event in Saudi Arabia. Netflix, Disney and Amazon are among platforms reportedly interested.
items.title: FIFA Opens Bidding for US Rights to 2030 World Cup

items.summary: According to a Fortune report, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan are shifting their philanthropic and corporate investments toward artificial intelligence, science and STEM education. The couple led $50 million to Sacramento State University for state-of-the-art STEM labs and an AI center, announced by California Governor Gavin Newsom on January 28 as part of a redevelopment plan turning three vacant Capitol Mall office buildings into a downtown campus. Zuckerberg said the investments would strengthen communities and support future leaders; Newsom added that students need affordable housing near where they study. The gift reflects a broader change at the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, which is directing most resources toward biomedical AI research through its Biohub network. CZI also laid off around 70 employees earlier this year as it streamlined operations.
items.title: Zuckerberg and Chan redirect giving toward AI and science

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on Sunday, October 25. In Varanasi he will inaugurate a garment manufacturing facility at around 11 a.m., witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 as Chief Guest, and later travel to Bhubaneswar to inaugurate the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute.
items.title: Modi To Visit Varanasi And Bhubaneswar On October 25

items.summary: Microsoft Research has open-sourced Agensh, a decentralized harness for large teams of coding agents that removes the central orchestrator common to most agent frameworks. Each worker independently claims sub-tasks via Gitea and Mattermost, shares findings on a shared board, verifies work against acceptance criteria, and merges into a common Git repo—running concurrently without a lead agent. On ProgramBench's five hardest tasks using GPT-5.6-sol at high reasoning effort, scaling from 1 to 8 agents added 1.37 points; the 5-task mean rose from 19.31% (1 agent) to 28.78% (128 agents). Speed also improved: on pandoc, 128 agents passed 30% at the 30-minute checkpoint versus 60 and 90 minutes for 32 and 8 agents. With GPT-6.1-sol, pandoc reached 79.59% with 32 agents—though these figures are not in the v1 paper.
items.title: Microsoft Research Open-Sources Agensh Multi-Agent Harness

items.summary: Ukraine says Starshield and Starlink are back to full speed after a week-long slowdown that left its defences exposed, with Zelenskyy confirming restoration overnight. Ukraine's defence ministry reported stable speeds over 400 kph. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk accused the Ukrainian military of violating terms by using it for offensive strikes. Beskrestnov said long-range drone use remains physically impossible at 70-90 kph.
items.title: Ukraine Restores Starlink Speeds; Musk Blames Kyiv

items.summary: Japanese carmakers are accelerating vehicle development timelines to compete with faster-moving Chinese rivals, which build new models in under two years versus the four to five years typical for Japanese firms. Nissan targets a 40% reduction through shared platforms and expects part types cut by 70%. Toyota’s Area 35 project aims to improve plant floor space use by 35%, while Suzuki plans development times around two years and Mitsubishi up to three years by roughly 2030.
items.title: Japanese Automakers Shorten Model Development Times Amid Chinese Competition

items.summary: Singapore's Straits Times market column reports that the Japanese yen surged against both the US dollar and euro, reaching a one-year high on Oct 23 amid global flight to safety. Disappointing technology and AI earnings plus Middle East tensions boosted demand for safe-haven assets. The piece also covers strong Q3 results from S-REITs including Keppel DC REIT (DPU up 11.7% year on year) and FCT, SGX chief Loh Boon Chye's decision to step down in mid-July 2027, and plantation firms responding to SGX haze queries. Figures are drawn from company filings and market data reported during the week.
items.title: Yen Hits One-Year High as SGX Chief Announces Departure

items.summary: The 19th EU-China Business and Technology Cooperation Fair concluded in Chengdu on October 23, drawing representatives from nearly 700 companies and institutions across more than 20 countries for face-to-face discussions. New energy, environmental protection, and intelligent robotics were among the key sectors highlighted as participants explored opportunities between European businesses and China.
items.title: 19th EU-China Fair Concludes in Chengdu With Nearly 700 Attendees

items.summary: Senior UN officials marked the 55th anniversary of China's restoration to its lawful United Nations seat by reaffirming their adherence to General Assembly Resolution 2758. Guy Ryder, UN under-secretary-general for policy, told CGTN that the organization continues to be guided by and will uphold the resolution consistently. Stephen Jackson, UN resident coordinator in China, called it a historic moment that eliminated possibilities of two Chinas or Taiwan independence and strengthened Global South representation on the Security Council. Adopted October 25, 1971 with an overwhelming majority at the UNGA's 26th session, the resolution restored all rights of the People's Republic of China.
items.title: UN officials reaffirm Resolution 2758 as China's seat turns 55

items.summary: The number of China-Europe freight train trips through the network's eastern corridor reached a record high this year, as goods increasingly shifted toward higher-value technology-intensive products. As of Friday, the corridor had handled 6,024 trips this year, up 40.3% year on year, marking the first time annual traffic surpassed 6,000 trips.
items.title: China-Europe freight trains hit record high on eastern corridor

items.summary: At the 29th Beijing Music Festival, director Zou Shuang presents The Magic Flute in an unexpected new setting. CGTN went beyond the stage to meet the international cast and creative team behind the production. They discussed the surprises shaping the staging and how modern Beijing is influencing their experience of Mozart's timeless opera.
items.title: Beijing Stages Mozart's Magic Flute With Modern Chinese Setting

items.summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw assured support for projects transforming Andhra Pradesh into a global semiconductor design hub, announced during Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu’s Saturday courtesy call in Delhi. Vaishnaw said the Centre would back research and development, skill training and capacity building, plus AI infrastructure. The two also discussed railway connectivity proposals.
items.title: Railways Minister Assures Andhra Pradesh Semiconductor Support

items.summary: The Federation of LPG Distributors of India (FLDI) has urged its members to continue supply and delivery operations in Delhi, opposing calls for protests and an indefinite strike. The FLDI said the concerns of distributors are being heard and that it had received assurances of an early resolution as Rahul Gandhi’s INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 raises disruption worries.
items.title: LPG distributor body urges members to keep supplying ahead of Gandhi rally

items.summary: President Donald Trump defended his use of tariffs at a campaign rally in Georgia, saying they have made the U.S. richer and that Volkswagen agreed to build a new $4.2 billion Audi plant there. He called it 'the single largest investment in U.S. auto industry history' and said without tariffs, companies would not be coming.
items.title: Trump Defends Tariffs as Audi Announces U.S. Plant

items.summary: The CBI registered an FIR against M/s IL&FS Energy Development Company Ltd and its top executives on Oct 21, following a complaint from Canara Bank’s Bandra circle office. Searches across Delhi, Mumbai and Noida seized incriminating documents. According to the CBI, the accused allegedly conspired to obtain a Rs 100 crore term loan and $50 million foreign currency loan, diverting funds through associate entities and causing an estimated wrongful loss of Rs 212.3 crore via conspiracy and cheating charges.
items.title: CBI files FIR against IL&FS Energy, top execs in Rs 212cr Canara Bank loan fraud case

items.summary: The item lists the winners of Emergent Ventures’ twentieth cohort in India, a group of engineers, students and self-taught builders who received grants for projects spanning manuscript digitization, AI assistants for shopkeepers, clinical tools for ADHD and cancer records, autonomous spacecraft technologies, air-water extraction machines, and regenerative-medicine biomaterials. Several recipients are teenagers or early-career researchers; one project aims to make graft designs 30–40% more affordable. The piece notes that unfamiliar readers can learn about Emergent Ventures through two links, directs them to the EV India announcement for this cohort’s details.
items.title: Emergent Ventures India awards grants to young founders and researchers

items.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement has taken into custody Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Kaushik at the Henderson Detention Centre in Nevada. According to Haryana Police, Bhau entered the US using a forged passport surname after fleeing India amid murder and extortion charges; discrepancies in his biometric data led investigators to identify him as wanted criminals. His criminal network is linked to several shootings across India. He faces deportation through cooperation with the CBI. The report also includes an unrelated profile of journalist Bobins at Live Mint.
items.title: ICE Detains Two Indian Gangsters in Las Vegas

items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority warned residents to stay alert as a depression over the east-central and southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by October 27. Managing Director Prakhar Jain cautioned against lowering guard, while the Meteorological Department projected further intensification toward a very severe cyclonic storm near the Andhra Pradesh coast around October 28.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh braces for intensifying Bay of Bengal depression

items.summary: At the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026 in Ahmedabad, India's men beat Uganda 44-30 and its women crushed Singapore 32-16 on Saturday. Shivam Patare led the raiding effort with eight points; Sakshi topped the women's attack with six. The victories highlighted balanced Indian raid and defence as teams prepare for Sunday matches against Uganda and Malaysia, per a press release auto-generated by an agency feed.
items.title: India Clinch Double Victory at Inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship

items.summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) alleged that slogans including “Free Umar Khalid” and “Long Live Naxalbari” were written on the walls of Delhi's Jawaharlal Nehru University, urging action against those responsible. The claims came two days after similar slogans were reportedly spotted at Jamia Millia Islamia University in the capital. ABVP JNU said the administration should identify offenders and take appropriate action to safeguard the campus atmosphere. The JNU administration has reportedly taken cognisance of the matter and is looking into it, saying it would not allow vested interests to disturb peace on the campus. Congress leader Imran Masood dismissed reports of “Free Kashmir” slogans at Jamia as fake news but acknowledged some posters carrying the slogan had been put up there. Tensions flared between teaching staff and students over disciplinary action amid ongoing protests about the restoration of the students' union, prompting the university to shift classes online.
items.title: ABVP Alleges Anti-India Slogans on JNU Walls and Demands Action

items.summary: The People's Action Party elected its next central executive committee at a conference on Oct 25, with cadres voting from a secret ballot of 19 candidates. First-term ministers Jeffrey Siow and Jasmin Lau were placed on the nomination list but were not voted in. Secretary-General Lawrence Wong said the party must earn continued support rather than rely on past mandates, warning that younger Singaporeans may feel less bond unless connected to them on their own terms.
items.title: PAP elects new central executive committee; Siow and Lau nominated but not voted in

items.summary: The Diamonds lead Australia's live blog opens with Australia trailing New Zealand 2-0 in game three of the Constellation Cup in Sydney. Coach Stacey Marinkovich says her team must win the first five minutes and play more disciplined netball after being penalised heavily, conceding 145 penalties to New Zealand's 100.
items.title: Australia trail New Zealand two games into Constellation Cup

items.summary: A three-day chase in the Tochigi capital of Utsunomiya ended when a zookeeper shot a bear with a tranquilizer gun near a private residence, an episode widely shown on TV and online. The incident is seen as part of a growing number of human–bear conflicts across Japan following last fiscal year’s record 238 attacks and 13 deaths nationwide. Experts warn of another pre-hibernation surge this fall but note rich acorn harvests may keep many bears well fed, likely limiting the worst outcomes.
items.title: Japan braces for more bear attacks after Utsunomiya hunt

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Congress alleges that during a special voter campaign, block-level officers filled and pre-filled Form 8 for voters whose details differed from their EPIC cards. The party says the discrepancies appeared after April's Special Intensive Revision list was released, making it the Election Commission's responsibility to correct them rather than burdening voters. Whistleblower Kumud Gangwar said forms were signed without acknowledgment slips or dates. Anas Khan accused EC staff of using Form 8 receipts to blame voters and cover up alleged vote theft.
items.title: UP Congress Alleges EC Used Form-8 To Cover Up Voter Discrepancies

items.summary: Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands protested across France on Saturday before some clashes late in the day, officials said. Police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse demonstrators in cities including Paris, while barricades burned in Marseille and a shop was ransacked in Bordeaux. Officials avoided rioting and looting at last weekend's scale. The interior ministry put Saturday's turnout at an estimated 410,000; unions said about 800,000. Some 70,000 police were deployed amid restrictions over cost-of-living and school grievances. President Macron had limited demonstrations to those led by recognised unions. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reported several thousand radical activists gathered at the march's rear, including around 500 identified as rioters, while nearly 1,000 arrests would rise further. Two people were seriously injured in Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand.
items.title: France Arrests Nearly 1,000 After Mass Protests Turn Violent

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is in Varanasi as the Indian Air Force marks its 94th Foundation Day with the finale of the 'Wings Over Ganges' air show at Namo Ghat. The display features Tejas, Rafale and Su-30 jets along with transport aircraft and helicopters. A Surya Kiran aerobatic team and Sarang display team are set to perform over the river Ganga during a 90-minute flypast watched by more than 12,000 spectators.
items.title: Modi Opens IAF Air Show in Varanasi

items.summary: A 25-year-old woman, seven months pregnant with twins and a resident of Utnoor, died on Saturday morning after being admitted to Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) in Adilabad. Her family alleged the staff neglected her worsening condition before she died from pulmonary embolism at 32 weeks of pregnancy. RIMS director Dr Rathod JaiSingh said a three-member committee would investigate.
items.title: Family Alleges Negligence After Pregnant Woman Dies at RIMS

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party alleged that a Congress worker named Shilpa voted under the name of Asha Patil during Karnataka's Haveri MLC elections, claiming she entered the booth with Minister Rudrappa Lamani. BJP MLA Mahesh Tenginkai shared video evidence and demanded legal action. Congress spokesperson Shripad Renu dismissed the claims as baseless fairy tales spun by the opposition.
items.title: BJP and Congress Clash Over Alleged Fake Voting in Karnataka Haveri MLC Polls

items.summary: KL Rahul scored just four runs across two innings for India A, who were bowled out for 113 before New Zealand A posted 317 to take a 204-run lead. In the second innings he was dismissed hit-wicket after edging a ball toward himself and striking his own off stump with his bat while trying to stop it; replays showed the wicket would not have fallen anyway. Fraser Sheat took both of Rahul's dismissals.
items.title: KL Rahul dismissed twice in India A loss

items.summary: In an exclusive interview with PTI, Air Chief Marshal Singh said the guiding principle for India's theatreisation should be 'centralised control' where necessary and 'decentralised execution' where appropriate. He cited ongoing conflicts worldwide to assert that air power can decisively shape military outcomes, quoting himself: 'Recent conflicts around the world have once again underlined how decisively air power can shape military outcomes.' Singh said transformation of this scale should be implemented in phases so operational readiness is never compromised, and warned against predicting future battlefields with excessive certainty. He noted progress has stalled due to divergent views among services over command structures.
items.title: IAF chief outlines guiding principles for theatreisation

items.summary: SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk said on X that the Ukrainian military breached Starlink's terms of service by using the satellite network to conduct offensive drone strikes. He stated that this loophole was closed last week and clarified that the civilian service was never intended for such use, while noting that the separate military-grade system Starshield remains under U.S. government control.
items.title: Musk Says Ukraine Violated Starlink Terms for Drone Strikes

items.summary: Australia’s federal police commissioner, Krissy Barrett, says politicians’ rhetoric is fuelling threats and abuse against leaders after MP Helen Haines was allegedly deliberately attacked outside her Wangaratta office. She remains serious but stable at the Alfred hospital following a double leg amputation. Barrett reports that threat summaries once read “pages and pages long,” links physical hate mail to online threats, and says she would challenge anyone calling such abuse free speech.
items.title: AFP Commissioner Links Political Rhetoric to Surge in Threats Against MPs

items.summary: AMMK General Secretary TTV Dhinakaran attacked the ruling Tamil Nadu government over soaring prices of essential commodities, warning that steep rice price increases could threaten the TVK government. He called it a “disaster” for voters and predicted its end soon. Quoting supporters, he said they united under Edappadi K Palaniswami to restore J Jayalalithaa’s Amma government to safeguard law and order.
items.title: Dhinakaran Warns Rising Rice Prices Could Threaten TVK Government

items.summary: A man has died following a workplace incident on a rural property near Shepparton in Victoria's north-east. Emergency services were called to Evans Road, Waggarandall, about 40 kilometres north-east of Shepparton, where the man was reported trapped under a loading ramp around 10:20am on Sunday. Advanced life support paramedics attended but he died at the scene. Police and SES also responded; police will report to the coroner.
items.title: Man dies after being crushed by ramp in northern Victoria

items.summary: Police in Fort Kochi registered a case against right-wing influencer Amrit Singh Darren over a video making communal allegations about the city, Kashi Art Café, and Kerala's Muslim community. The Ernakulam district committee of the Muslim Youth League lodged a complaint seeking stringent action, while the Democratic Youth Federation of India also condemned the remarks. Chief Minister VD Satheesan said attempts to divide communities would not be tolerated, and opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan accused the Sangh Parivar of outsourcing hate through online provocateurs.
items.title: Kochi hate video prompts police case and political condemnations

items.summary: Young Indian protesters in Delhi have drawn on historical freedom struggles, notably the Quit India Movement of 1942 and events from 1919 and 1928, to frame their opposition to police actions during demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Students such as Devyani Sarkar, Neha Bora, Kriti Gupta, Annapurna, and Shubhit Kumar compared current repression—detentions of students and Opposition leaders—to British colonial rule, with one protester invoking Bhagat Singh’s line about replacing “white” colonizers with “black” ones. Comedian Shamik Chakrabarti dubbed Imran Khan’s expulsion from India ‘Quit India Movement 2’, while the Cockroach Janta Party timed a Mumbai protest to Gandhi’s birth anniversary and framed it as a mass jail campaign. The article presents these comparisons as symbolic resonance, not verified claims of government intent.
items.title: Indian protesters invoke colonial-era movements amid Delhi unrest

items.summary: A purported audio recording alleging a Rs 500-crore payment to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange has ignited one of Maharashtra’s biggest political controversies, exposing tensions within the ruling Mahayuti alliance. The row began after Jarange released the recording and denied receiving any money, claiming it exposed a conspiracy against him. Allegations that funds were routed through Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde drew sharp responses: BJP officials called it fake and AI-generated, while Shiv Sena leaders accused Jarange of colluding with BJP elements to target Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered a forensic investigation into the clip’s authenticity and origins.
items.title: Maharashtra leaders clash over disputed Rs 500-crore audio clip

items.summary: Manila police are investigating a laptop and child abuse images found in the former home of Meghan Markle's estranged father, Thomas Markle. Interior minister Jonvic Remulla told AFP that forensic results would arrive within a week and that appropriate legal action could follow if evidence is sufficient; Markle denies all claims. British tabloid the Sun first reported it.
items.title: Philippines Investigates Laptop Found at Thomas Markle's Former Home

items.summary: The Kargil Democratic Alliance rejected the Union government’s October 15 draft governance framework for Ladakh, reported by The New Indian Express, saying it gives overriding authority to the lieutenant governor and bureaucracy while leaving little power with the proposed elected body. Talks have stalled after a May meeting; co-convener Asgar Karbalai said an earlier agreement had promised legislative, executive and financial powers plus Article 371-K safeguards, but the draft instead places governance under Article 240. Co-convener Sajjad Kargili called it “an attack on the rights of the people of this region.” The alliance warned of protests if agreed terms are not implemented.
items.title: Ladakh Leaders Reject Draft Governance Framework Over L-G Powers

items.summary: Audi plans a roughly $4.2 billion investment in Macon, Georgia, creating about 4,500 jobs with capacity for up to 200,000 vehicles annually and production targeted for the early 2030s, Audi said. Chairman Gernot Döllner announced it alongside Trump at a Perry rally, where he called it proof his trade policy draws manufacturing home. The move arrives amid competitive Georgia Senate and governor races ahead of midterm elections.
items.title: Audi's Georgia Plant Investment Becomes Trump Campaign Symbol

items.summary: The UK government announced that more than £1bn would be provided in the upcoming Budget for social and affordable housing in England, pushing total funding for its 10-year homes programme past £40bn. Mayors and regional leaders are expected to receive greater powers, transitional seed funding of an initial £285m next year, and a new £1.5bn borrowing facility from 2028. Chancellor John Healey said cities would get the right to decide their own future. Separately, reports suggest billions in defence spending may be unveiled, prompting shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith to call for Healey's resignation over plans to reach 3% of GDP on defence by 2030.
items.title: Healey's Budget to Fund £1bn for Social and Affordable Housing

items.summary: Kim Aris, son of Aung San Suu Kyi, said after an eight-year-gap phone call that his 81-year-old mother appears mentally and physically well yet lives in near-complete isolation. He described her as effectively held in solitary confinement with no contact beyond military or police figures, and uncertain whether she is located at a fenced residence in Naypyidaw. Aris characterised recent government photographs of her as public-relations stunts rather than evidence of fair treatment. He said international support for her has dwindled since the 2016-2017 Rohingya crisis and that she remains shut off from news, though he noted her past statements on the issue could fill volumes. The article places this within Myanmar's 2021 military coup and a civil war that conflict monitors say has killed more than 100,000 people.
items.title: Suu Kyi's son says she is healthy but isolated

items.summary: A newsletter opens by explaining that humans prefer right angles through a trait called grid sensitivity, citing researcher Dinesh Katre and the Harappans' 4,000-year-old cities. It then turns to a heist in California where thieves broke into a FedEx truck outside Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) and stole graded Pokémon cards worth around $963,000. The piece traces rising card prices through nostalgia, the pandemic, and speculation—mentioning Logan Paul's Pikachu flip from over $5 million to $16.5 million—and notes PSA deactivated the stolen cards' certification numbers after the robbery. It closes with a reader-recommended book by Jeet Thayil.
items.title: Why thieves target graded Pokémon cards, and why rectangles rule

items.summary: Cognition has released Devin Vulnerability Fixes, a free, open-source set of three agent skills under the MIT license that find and patch vulnerable PHP, Node.js and self-managed GitLab deployments. The plugin targets three critical remote code execution advisories: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), the October 2026 Node.js release covering 10 CVEs and self-managed GitLab bug CVE-2026-110264 rated CVSS 10.0. It runs in Devin and other coding agents that read SKILL.md files, following a five-step workflow of inventory, approval, verification, testing before and after, and one pull request per repository. Cognition packaged the remediation workflow it used internally; no published fix-rate benchmark exists, as results depend on test coverage.
items.title: Cognition Releases Open-Source Plugin for Critical RCE Vulnerabilities

items.summary: Police clashed with protesters in Paris after a largely peaceful day of demonstrations turned violent on Saturday night, as crowds threw objects and fireworks at officers. Around 70,000 police were deployed across France for a second consecutive weekend, using tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds. The Interior Ministry estimated around 400,000 people took part in Saturday's demonstrations, with nearly 1,000 arrests made.
items.title: Protesters and Police Clash in Paris After Nightfall Unrest

items.summary: Syria is pursuing a broad energy-sector revival as part of post-conflict reconstruction, with the transitional government now controlling key assets including the Omar oil field and Tabiyeh gas complex. Wood Mackenzie figures indicate conflict-related output declines: oil production down 80 per cent and gas by half from pre-war levels of 380,000 bpd crude and 900 million cubic feet of gas. The government has signed deals with Chevron, Qatar’s UCC Holding, the Syrian Petroleum Company, ACWA Power, Marv Energy, and a $7 billion consortium to expand oil, gas, solar, wind, and hydropower capacity. Analysts note potential as an energy trade hub amid Strait of Hormuz restrictions, per the Baker Institute.
items.title: Syria Pursues Energy Sector Revival After Conflict Damage

items.summary: On the last day of campaigning, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro held their closing rallies on Saturday in Rio de Janeiro, one day after a combative final television debate. Opinion polls show them neck and neck, with around 20% of voters having abstained in the first round, where Bolsonaro won 47% over Lula's 45%. After three weeks of intense campaigning, the incumbent appears to have regained ground from his low approval rating of 24%, while Bolsonaro faces scrutiny over a bribery admission and ongoing investigations.
items.title: Brazilian candidates hold final rallies before runoff election

items.summary: Ukraine said Saturday that its Starlink satellite system and military's Starshield were back to high operating speeds after more than a week of disruptions. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attributed the restoration to direct dialogue, while Ukrainian officials believe U.S. government pressure caused the earlier restrictions. Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara noted connectivity now exceeds 250 mph, up from about 100 mph during the outage.
items.title: Ukraine Reports Starlink and Starshield Speeds Restored

items.summary: Days before Israel's election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major military operation in the West Bank city of Hebron after two soldiers were killed and three wounded at a checkpoint. The Israeli military said it was searching for militants and weapons near Friday's attack site. Local officials estimate around 250 families have been displaced, though Governor Khaled Dudin put the number lower at 150.
items.title: Netanyahu Orders Large-Scale Hebron Evictions After Soldier Deaths

items.summary: BJP leaders on Friday condemned National Conference president Farooq Abdullah after his reported remarks questioned India's intentions toward Kashmir and suggested Pakistan was pressuring New Delhi by raising the issue internationally. Sat Sharma demanded an apology, while Arjun Munda called the comments condemnable and Amar Kumar Bauri defended Centre policies citing development initiatives following the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A.
items.title: BJP Leaders Condemn Farooq Abdullah Over Kashmir Remarks

items.summary: Rupert Lowe, leader of Britain's far-right Restore Britain party, said Saturday the UK owes no country 'unconditional' support after a report that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered backing for Argentina in its sovereignty dispute over the Falkland Islands. Lowe wrote on X that British interests should guide foreign policy alone and added the islands will remain British.
items.title: Restore Britain Leader Questions Unconditional Support for Israel

items.summary: The Metropolitan Police confirmed it received a letter in January 2019 containing claims about alleged offending outside the UK, but did not share details with other agencies. The force is considering referring itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct over its handling. Meghan said she was deeply distressed by allegations concerning her father Thomas Markle; he denies possessing images and remains under investigation in the Philippines.
items.title: Met Police Confirm Receipt of Allegations Against Thomas Markle

items.summary: The Janata Dal (United), or JD(U), expelled Mokama MLA Anant Kumar Singh and his wife Neelam Devi for six years on Saturday, citing alleged anti-party activities, indiscipline and campaigning against the party's candidate in the Bihar Legislative Council elections. In an order issued by president Umesh Singh Kushwaha, the party cancelled both leaders' primary memberships and recommended that the Assembly Speaker cancel Singh's membership under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution. The couple had backed a Jan Suraaj Party candidate over JD(U)'s nominee Neeraj Kumar Singh. Expulsion from the party is separate from any disqualification process. Singh, who returned to the JD(U) for the 2025 Assembly election, has declared 28 criminal cases in his affidavit. He dismissed earlier remarks about nine people being murdered as refuted by Sanjay Kumar Jha of the working president's office keyphrases [
items.title: JD(U) Expels Singh and Wife Over Election Row

items.summary: European student protests have spread across Europe, and in Serbia they are channeling the movement into Sunday's parliamentary elections through a list of candidates drawn from academics, economists, athletes and engineers rather than career politicians. The Student List positions itself as the most serious challenge yet to Aleksandar Vucic, who has led since 2012 after taking power following the Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse that killed sixteen people two years ago. Around 150,000 attended a recent rally in Belgrade's Slavija Square. Analysts note Vucic remains defiant and accused of dominating media through state resources, but observers say the election now looks uncertain for the first time in 14 years.
items.title: Serbian Students Turn Protests Into Election Challenge

items.summary: Vietnam’s government ordered provincial and municipal authorities to introduce support policies for households installing self-consumption rooftop solar systems by the end of December 2026, under Government Office Dispatch No. 10790/VPCP-CN dated Oct. 22. The Ministry of Industry and Trade must propose deployment targets with installation capacities and commissioning schedules, prioritizing northern provinces facing supply constraints. Vietnam Electricity reported 134,410 rooftop solar installations totaling more than 11.45 GW at the end of August 2026.
items.title: Vietnam Orders Provinces to Add Rooftop Solar Incentives by December 2026

items.summary: A Guardian review of freedom-of-information data found that most UK levelling up projects are still not finished, years after funds were allocated. Of 1,347 funded projects examined, 821 remained unfinalised as of May this year, and 73 council areas had completed none at all. Jack Shaw of Groundwork Research said the figures reveal a large gap between ambition and delivery. Zoë Billingham of IPPR North criticised short-term funding pots, while Sarah Longlands warned Labour's Pride in Place programme could face similar delays. The government responded that long-term targeted funding would support local communities.
items.title: UK levelling up projects remain largely unfinished years after funding

items.summary: The UK government has launched the pride in place programme, allocating £20m to North East Lincolnshire council for regeneration of its struggling town centre. Residents report visible improvements, including a new cinema and community spaces, yet many remain doubtful about whether funding will meaningfully address deep-rooted decline driven by online shopping, industrial collapse and out-of-town retail parks. Neela Parker Talwar of the Centre for Cities argues that £20m is not so much money and cannot fund major projects like buying large empty buildings. She warns that causes such as access to jobs may lie beyond local authority reach. Some residents instead place their hope in a stronger local economy rather than government schemes.
items.title: Pride in Place scheme faces scepticism over Grimsby's high street revival

items.summary: According to EnergySage's Home Electrification Marketplace Report, U.S. residential solar prices rose 3.2% in the first half of 2026 to a median $2.57/W, up from $2.49/W six months earlier. The increase followed the expiration of the federal tax credit and higher labor costs. Third-party ownership financing grew sharply as installers sought alternatives after the Section 25D credit ended in late 2025, with installer quotes for such products rising to about 41%. EnergySage cautioned that long-term savings from newer pre-paid offerings remain unestablished, and noted its findings reflect marketplace quotes rather than a full census of installations.
items.title: U.S. Residential Solar Prices Rise as Third-Party Ownership Grows

items.summary: Volkswagen is introducing the ID. Unyx 09 electric sedan in China, developed through its partnership with XPENG to compete against domestic EV makers amid industry struggles there. The car offers a CLTC range of 755 km (469 miles) and costs from 179,900 yuan ($26,939) for the Ultra version up to 249,900 yuan ($37,421) for the Max. It uses a VLA driving system from XPENG and an LFP battery from CATL.
items.title: Volkswagen Launches ID. Unyx 09 in China With XPENG Partnership

items.summary: A CleanTechnica author argues that the Trump administration's war on Iran has caused or revealed a seismic shift in global oil markets, making demand elastic for the first time. The piece notes EIA and IEA projections of over 2 million barrels per day decline in consumption by 2026, which would be unprecedented without an economic crisis. Analyzing gasoline prices above $4 adjusted for inflation across five historical periods, the author concludes high fuel costs did not reduce demand until 2026, suggesting price sensitivity has increased. The hypothesis remains untested and is offered openly for debate, with the author attributing accelerated transition to a post-oil world partly to Trump's policies.
items.title: CleanTechnica Author Proposes Oil Demand Is Becoming Elastic Amid Iran Conflict

items.summary: Nicole Sanchotene, project coordinator at NetLab (UFRJ), told Global Voices that big tech companies’ transparency and cooperation policies during Brazil’s 2026 election amount to ‘governance washing.’ She says platforms like Kwai—over 60 million users—and Meta do not fully comply with electoral norms. Users report sudden drops in Instagram Stories views after political posts; journalist Leandro Demori showed his fell from about one million or 400,000 views to 9,000 (s34). On October 16, Meta admitted technical problems affecting pro-Lula content delivery but denied bias, citing ‘global technical glitches’ and anti-fraud measures (s4,s3). Lula filed a complaint; the electoral court ordered equal treatment. Sanchotene stresses algorithms are opaque black boxes with no oversight, and that candidates may be running under unequal conditions—a global issue repeated across elections.
items.title: Brazilian Expert Calls Big Tech Transparency Policies 'Governance Washing'

items.summary: Royal Darwin Hospital has apologised to around a dozen pregnant patients after confidential medical information was shared publicly online. A 'medical observer' associated with the hospital posted images and videos of handover sheets containing patient details, including names, record numbers, ward locations and clinical histories, to an Instagram account that had 28,000 followers. RDH management said NT Health had been informed and confirmed the doctor's attachment was terminated. Dr Neda Mogharehabed could not confirm how or where the images originated but said she did not intend to disclose patient information. ABC Radio Darwin producer Shanelle Tobin, who is 17 weeks pregnant, said learning her details were shared publicly caused distress. The Australian Medical Association called any breach of confidentiality unacceptable and urged RDH to improve staff training on social media use.
items.title: Royal Darwin Hospital Apologises for Patient Data Posted on Instagram

items.summary: The Western Railway Mazdoor Sangh has demanded a high-level inquiry after three ticket collectors aboard the Delhi-Mumbai Garib Rath Express were allegedly assaulted by intoxicated passengers who reportedly snatched their inspection machines. The union, which raised the matter with railway officials and police, also called for CCTV footage review amid broader concerns over assaults on staff.
